title: Tibble's Sunny Gift
markdown:
In the Wobblecap Mountains, where the soft mist glowed like pearls and the trees hummed quiet songs to the wind, lived a little goblin named Tibble. His home was a burrow, snug and warm like a big hug, lined with the softest, bounciest moss. It always smelled a little like sweet moon-blossoms. And always, always with Tibble, was Mumble, his round and fluffy marmot. Mumble’s fur was the colour of warm honey on a sunny day. His little nose wiggled with happy, gentle wonder as he looked at the world with Tibble.

One soft morning, the sun stretched long, golden arms over the mountaintops. It painted the dewdrops on the leaves with shiny light. Tibble held a small parcel. He had wrapped it with a leaf as blue as a summer sky. He tied it with a thread from a spider's web, which twinkled like tiny morning dewdrops. Inside, Tibble knew, was a little piece of sunshine. It was a warm smile he had saved just for this moment. This little parcel was for his dear friend, Willow Whisker. She lived a little way through the ferny trees, where the leaves always seemed to dance.

"Mumble, my little marmot," Tibble whispered. His voice was soft and gentle, like leaves rustling in a summer breeze. "It’s time. Time to take this special sunshine to Willow Whisker. She will love it so." Mumble, who knew Tibble's heart, gave a happy, soft rumble. His little tail thumped gently on the soft floor of their burrow. Tibble smiled a wide, happy smile. His bright eyes smiled too. The smallest parcels, he thought with a happy sigh, can hold the biggest, warmest feelings of love. This one surely did.

Tibble tucked the special parcel into a little woven bag that hung from his shoulder. With Mumble trotting close beside him, they stepped out of their cosy burrow. The air outside was cool and sweet. It smelled like damp earth after a gentle rain and fresh, wild mint. They walked into the ferny grove. The tall, pale birch trees swayed, looking like soft moonlight on rippling water. Sunlight played through the green leaves, making pretty, shifting patterns on the soft, mossy ground.

"Oh, Mumble," Tibble said softly, his voice full of quiet wonder. "Isn't this path lovely? Look at the smooth pebbles, so nice for rolling. And the leaves are singing a gentle, peaceful song as they sway." Mumble waddled along happily. His little paws made soft sounds on the velvety moss. His nose wiggled at every new, interesting smell on the gentle air. They listened together to the quiet hum of the forest. It was a peaceful song sung by tiny crickets and the soft whisper of breezes playing in the leaves.

As they walked, following a path marked by tiny flowers that nodded hello, they came to a lovely, sunlit clearing. In the middle of the clearing was a big kitchen. Smoke curled happily from its chimney, smelling warm and yummy. Standing just outside was a very big, very gentle ogre named Crumbleton. Crumbleton was known in the mountains not for his size, but for his kind hands and his warm, welcoming ways. He looked at cabbages as round as the moon, carrots as long as Tibble's arm, and plump tomatoes that seemed to hold the sun's warmth.

"Hello there, little ones!" Crumbleton boomed. His voice was like warm honey rolling gently downhill. It was deep and kind. His smile crinkled his kind eyes and made his whole big face light up. "What a lovely day for a walk! Who might you be, little travellers?"

Tibble held Mumble a little closer. His heart felt warm and safe. He smiled back. "Hello, Crumbleton! We are Tibble and Mumble. We are going to see our friend Willow Whisker. We have a special parcel for her."

Crumbleton nodded slowly. His large hands moved with surprising gentleness. "Ah, Willow! She is a sweet soul and a good friend. My, what a happy little parcel! It looks as bright as a summer morning." He showed with a wide, gentle hand towards his welcoming kitchen. "I've just baked some berry buns. They are still warm and smell very sweet, like a hug in a bun. Would you and your little marmot like to share one before you go on your way? It would make an old ogre happy."

Tibble's nose twitched with joy. The smell of warm berries and sweet, baking dough was one of the loveliest smells in the world. "Oh, yes please, Crumbleton!" Tibble chirped. His voice was full of happy excitement. "That would be wonderful! Mumble would love one too." Mumble gave a little rumble of happy agreement. His eyes were wide and bright with waiting.

Crumbleton carefully picked a bun, golden and plump. Its top shone a little. He gently broke off a small piece for Tibble. He broke off a tiny, perfect bit for Mumble. The bun was so soft and wonderfully warm. It was full of sweet, juicy berries that melted in his mouth. Tibble felt a gentle warmth spread through him. It was a quiet happiness, as comforting and safe as being under a soft, warm blanket. Mumble munched happily on his little piece. His little marmot tummy rumbled with pure happiness. They sat for a quiet moment, enjoying the peace of the clearing. They felt the warm sun on their faces and tasted the sweet berry bun. This quiet moment, Tibble thought with a happy sigh, was like a little pause in the day, a moment of pure, simple peace to keep.

With many happy thank yous to Crumbleton for his kindness and his wonderful buns, Tibble and Mumble continued their gentle walk. The path wound softly on, through more whispering birch trees and soft, green ferns that tickled Tibble’s knees. The little parcel felt warm against his side in his bag, carrying its special sunshine all the way to Willow Whisker. Soon, they saw a small, cheerful house nestled among tall, colourful flowers that nodded in the gentle breeze. It was Willow Whisker’s home.

Tibble skipped to the little wooden door and gently knocked. Willow Whisker, a squirrel with the softest, greyest fur and the brightest eyes that twinkled like little stars, opened the door. "Tibble! And Mumble too! What a lovely, lovely surprise!"

"Hello, Willow!" Tibble chirped. His heart felt light and happy, like a little bird flying. "We have a little parcel for you, a special sunny surprise!" He carefully took it from his bag and gave it to her.

Willow Whisker’s bright eyes widened with wonder as she gently took the leaf-wrapped parcel. "Oh, Tibble! It feels so warm! It feels like pure sunshine!" She carefully untied the twinkling thread and opened the leaf. Inside, on a bed of soft moss, was a tiny, smooth stone. It had a cheerful, bright sun painted on it. It seemed to glow with its own soft, golden light.

Willow Whisker held the little painted stone in her soft paws. Her eyes shimmered with a gentle, quiet happiness. "Oh, Tibble! It's beautiful. It's like you bottled up a whole day of happiness for me. Thank you, thank you so much!" She gave Tibble a warm, happy smile that made his own smile grow even bigger. Mumble wiggled happily, feeling the wonderful joy and love all around.

As the sky began to soften into pretty colours of purple and pink, Tibble, Mumble, and Willow sat together just outside Willow’s cosy door. They watched as the first shy stars began to twinkle in the darkening, soft sky. The little parcel of sunshine had brought a big, warm smile. Now, all three of them felt warm and peaceful and very happy. The mountain air was growing cool and nice. A gentle, quiet calm settled over the grove. Tibble snuggled Mumble close, feeling his soft fur. Willow tucked the little sun-stone carefully into her soft fur, close to her heart. Everything was just right, and soon, with sleepy sighs that sounded like happy sighs, they were all ready to dream sweet, gentle dreams until the morning sun peeked over the mountains again.
